q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most: 18 of 52 videos with a baseline (35%) beat their channel's norm, versus 9 of 39 for mid (23%) and just 1 of 19 for large (5%). The large-channel figure rests on a small n, so treat it cautiously.

Audiences are broadly happy, but unevenly. Net sentiment on product-side comments:
- Mid: +33 (53% positive, 20% negative), n=452 comments across 39 videos
- Small: +26 (48% positive, 22% negative), n=688 comments across 64 videos
- Large: +11 (43% positive, 32% negative), n=282 comments across 24 videos

So small channels break out most with solidly positive audiences, mid channels are the happiest, and large channels are the weakest on both measures. Caveat: these are comment samples, and the patterns are associations, not causes.
sql:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT c.video_id,
    CASE WHEN cr.tier LIKE 'nano%' OR cr.tier LIKE 'micro%' THEN 'small'
         WHEN cr.tier LIKE 'mid%' THEN 'mid'
         WHEN cr.tier LIKE 'macro%' OR cr.tier LIKE 'mega%' THEN 'large' END AS size_group,
    p.outperformer, p.rel_lift
  FROM content c
  JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id = c.channel_id
  JOIN performance p ON p.video_id = c.video_id
  WHERE c.topic = 'duo' AND c.format != 'official'
),
lift AS (
  SELECT size_group,
    COUNT(*) AS n_videos,
    COUNT(outperformer) AS n_with_baseline,
    SUM(outperformer) AS n_outperformers,
    ROUND(AVG(outperformer), 3) AS outperformer_rate,
    ROUND(AVG(rel_lift), 3) AS avg_rel_lift
  FROM v GROUP BY size_group
),
sent AS (
  SELECT v.size_group,
    COUNT(*) AS n_product_side_comments,
    COUNT(DISTINCT cm.video_id) AS n_videos_with_comments,
    ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment = 'positive'), 3) AS pct_positive,
    ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment = 'negative'), 3) AS pct_negative,
    ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment = 'positive') - AVG(cm.sentiment = 'negative'), 3) AS net_sentiment
  FROM comments cm
  JOIN v ON v.video_id = cm.video_id
  WHERE cm.lang = 'en' AND cm.trivial = 0
    AND cm.target IN ('product', 'price_value', 'competitor')
  GROUP BY v.size_group
)
SELECT l.size_group, l.n_videos, l.n_with_baseline, l.n_outperformers, l.outperformer_rate, l.avg_rel_lift,
  s.n_product_side_comments, s.n_videos_with_comments, s.pct_positive, s.pct_negative,
  CASE WHEN s.n_product_side_comments >= 10 THEN s.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment
FROM lift l LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size_group = l.size_group
ORDER BY l.outperformer_rate DESC
LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions work best for mid-sized channels. In 18 videos, 44% outperformed their baseline (about 8 of 18), with an average relative lift of 2.4. Product-side net sentiment was +37 (55% positive, 18% negative, n=230 comments).

Other formats trail:
- Explainer/tips: 17% outperformed (n=6 videos), lift 1.1, net sentiment +20 (n=70).
- Upgrade advice: no outperformers (n=6), lift 0.65, but sentiment was warm at +46 (63% positive, 17% negative, n=54).
- Comparison, keynote recap, meme short and "other": none outperformed, but each has only 1-3 videos, so I wouldn't read anything into them.

Caveat: these are associations from small samples, and only first impressions has a meaningful n.
sql: WITH v AS (SELECT c.video_id, c.format, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M'), perf AS (SELECT format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(CASE WHEN outperformer IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift FROM v GROUP BY format), sent AS (SELECT v.format, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(1.0*SUM(cm.sentiment='positive')/COUNT(*),3) AS pct_pos, ROUND(1.0*SUM(cm.sentiment='negative')/COUNT(*),3) AS pct_neg, ROUND(1.0*(SUM(cm.sentiment='positive')-SUM(cm.sentiment='negative'))/COUNT(*),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments cm JOIN v ON v.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') GROUP BY v.format) SELECT perf.format, perf.n_videos, perf.n_with_baseline, perf.outperformer_rate, perf.avg_rel_lift, sent.n_product_side, CASE WHEN sent.n_product_side>=10 THEN sent.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment, sent.pct_pos, sent.pct_neg FROM perf LEFT JOIN sent ON sent.format=perf.format ORDER BY perf.outperformer_rate DESC, perf.avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
The most negative high-lift videos are only mildly negative, and both are from Shawn Shaman.

1. The meme short "Apple Tricked You With iPhone Duo" has a net sentiment of -7 (43% positive, 50% negative, n=14). Its lift is 118.44 (relative lift 9.5) on 181,213 views.

2. The upgrade-advice video "Don't Buy The #iPhoneDuo... Here's Why" has a net sentiment of 0 (31% positive, 31% negative, n=16). Its lift is 135.84 (relative lift 10.9) on 207,835 views.

The sample is small, with only 14 and 16 product-side comments each, so a few comments could shift these scores. Also, no video in this top-lift group has clearly negative sentiment. The next three score 0 to +8.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT cm.video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(cm.sentiment='positive') AS pos, AVG(cm.sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments cm WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY cm.video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10) SELECT c.title, cr.name AS creator, c.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, p.outperformer, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pos-s.neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC LIMIT 5

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
The largest topics are Praise for the video (n=208, 12.8% of topic comments), Samsung Fold comparisons (n=141, 8.7%), and Cases and design (n=113, 6.9%).

Samsung Fold comparisons is the standout grower. It rose from 15 comments to 68 week over week (about 3.5x), the biggest absolute gain at +53. Cases and design (+39) and Praise for the video (+42) also added a lot.

By percentage growth, the leaders are:
- Apple Pencil support: 1 to 12 comments
- Fold animation: 1 to 7
- Buy or don't buy: 6 to 33
- Left-handed concerns: 4 to 22
- Apps and multitasking: 4 to 19

Caveat: the top percentage jumps start from very small bases (Apple Pencil and Fold animation had only 1 comment the prior week), so treat them as early signals. This is also a comment sample.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.topic_id IS NOT NULL), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM base), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS t FROM base), agg AS (SELECT b.topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(CASE WHEN b.d > mx.m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, SUM(CASE WHEN b.d <= mx.m-7 AND b.d > mx.m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev_week FROM base b, mx GROUP BY b.topic_id) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(1.0*a.n_total/tot.t,3) AS share_of_topic_comments, a.n_this_week, a.n_prev_week, a.n_this_week - a.n_prev_week AS abs_change, CASE WHEN a.n_prev_week>0 THEN ROUND(1.0*(a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week)/a.n_prev_week,3) END AS wow_growth FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id, tot ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
a:
Duo's audience is clearly more positive than any other topic: net sentiment is +26 (n=1,422 product-side comments across 127 videos), with 49% positive and 23% negative.

The other topics trail well behind:
- Competitor foldable: 0 net (n=25, 2 videos), 36% positive and 36% negative.
- Other: -10 net (n=51, 6 videos), 31% positive and 41% negative.
- Event general: -15 net (n=76, 8 videos), 26% positive and 41% negative.
- iPhone 18 Pro: 0 net, but n=4 from one video, so too small to read anything into.

Caveat: the non-Duo topics rest on far smaller samples than Duo, so their scores are less stable. Treat the gap as a clear direction, not a precise size.
sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, COUNT(DISTINCT m.video_id) AS n_videos, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN 'ok' ELSE 'n<10' END AS n_check FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY net_sentiment DESC LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
Commenters like the fold animation most. Its net sentiment is +70 (n=56, 84% positive), the strongest of any topic. Eagerness to buy is also well liked at +38 (n=104). Comparisons with Samsung's Fold get the most positive comments (79 of n=141, net +31).

The sharpest criticism is about price: net +14 (n=103), with 33% negative, the highest negative share among the larger topics. Next is Duo versus iPhone 18 Pro Max, net +2 (n=101, 32% negative), where positives and negatives nearly cancel out. "Reasons not to buy" is net +6 but small (n=55). Samsung comparisons also draw the most negative comments in raw count (36), because the topic is so big.

Caveat: even the most criticised topics are net positive. Topics overlap, so one comment can count in several, and this is a comment sample.
sql: WITH c AS (SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, cm.sentiment FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=cm.topic_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND t.pool='product' AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor')), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, name, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS n_neg, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='positive'),3) AS pos_share, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='negative'),3) AS neg_share FROM c GROUP BY topic_id, name), liked AS (SELECT 'most_liked' AS side, * FROM agg ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8), crit AS (SELECT 'most_criticised' AS side, * FROM agg ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8) SELECT * FROM liked UNION ALL SELECT * FROM crit LIMIT 40
